## 開篇固定收益主論點

能源價格再度飆升，加上美國財政部回購方案規模不足以滿足市場最積極的預期，美債全線下跌。10年期殖利率上升5.2個基點至4.842%，創2023年以來最高；5年期上升5.3個基點至4.617%，2年期上升3.7個基點至4.432%，30年期則上升4.4個基點至5.29%。

美國與伊朗衝突再次升級，率先引發美債賣壓；財政部隨後宣布，9月10日回購流通在外10至20年期債券的上限為$60億，使跌勢加劇。這項額度雖為原定規模的三倍，仍低於市場猜測單次操作可能達到$80億至$100億。油價上漲強化聯準會升息預期，初期由較短天期殖利率領漲；回購公告令人失望後，賣壓轉由長天期主導。

殖利率曲線因此小幅趨陡，有別於前一交易日遭遇油價衝擊時的趨平走勢。2年與10年期利差擴大1.5個基點至41個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大0.7個基點至85.8個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升4個基點至2.455%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升1.2個基點至2.387%。官方支持不如預期、政府與企業融資量龐大，且貨幣政策可能採取更強回應，促使投資人要求更高的實質補償；能源衝擊加劇也推升通膨補償。

需求良好的$390億10年期公債標售一度打斷跌勢，卻未能扭轉行情。得標殖利率為4.834%，是2007年以來最高標售殖利率，但較標售前市場殖利率低約1.5個基點，顯示當殖利率升至這個水準時已有買盤進場。標售後美債收斂跌幅，全日殖利率仍普遍上升3至5個基點。結果顯示，買方願意按當前殖利率承接利率風險；但先前市場對回購的反應也表明，財政部僅因擴大買進舊債，並不足以讓民間需求接受較低的市場出清殖利率。

另一股壓力來自能源市場。美軍摧毀伊朗油輪、中國恢復採購原油後，布蘭特原油期貨上漲4.22%至$102.05，WTI上漲4.28%至$97.01。對央行而言，比原油漲幅更重要的是成品油供應遠為吃緊。中東衝突及針對俄羅斯煉油廠的攻擊，使成品油出口估計每日減少400萬桶，歐洲柴油期貨相對布蘭特原油的每桶溢價因此升至約$75，年初僅約$21。

風險資產的反應仍有秩序，未陷入失控。標普500指數下跌0.48%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.29%，VIX上升4.71%至16.46。美國財政部長貝森特加大施壓、要求日本收緊政策，日圓隨之升值，美元指數部分受此影響小跌0.06%至98.783。黃金期貨上漲1.15%至每盎司$4,444.60。儘管美債下跌且新債發行繁多，美國投資級債利差仍明顯收窄；高收益債利差小幅擴大，硬通貨新興市場債利差則小幅收窄。

當日行情因而同時檢驗了債市兩種承接能力。財政部的干預對抑制長期殖利率所起作用不如投資人預期，但在整體借款成本上升後，公債標售與企業初級市場仍吸引大量需求。這並非融資市場失靈，而是通膨、貨幣政策、財政供給及科技相關資本支出競逐同一批債券承接能力時，市場要求更高補償。

## 回購規模不如預期，美債殖利率升至多年高點

財政部8月突然調整回購時程後，已承諾把數次長天期回購原有的$20億上限至少提高一倍。第一項明確擴大的操作，是把9月10日10至20年期券種的回購上限提高至$60億。至11月5日為止，另有六次10至30年期名目債券回購，上限均將至少達到$40億；確切規模通常會在每次操作前不久公布。

相較現行計畫，這些金額相當可觀；但貝森特公開推動壓低長期借款成本後，市場期待已被拉高，宣布的額度遂顯得有限。貝森特曾把擴大回購描述為替債市「退燒」，策略師因此設想單次買進規模可能高達$100億。相較於回購實際減少流通在外非當期券的機械性效果，預期與公告金額之間的落差對市場影響更大。

$60億也是以面額計算。許多合格舊債的交易價格低於面額，因此財政部實際投入的現金可能少於公布的上限。財政部進行長天期名目債券回購時，通常會買滿公告額度，但並無義務如此；操作當日的最終公告也可取代初步規模。

市場反應說明了回購能做什麼、又不能做什麼。回購可以改善交易較不活絡券種的流動性，讓交易商或投資人把舊券換成新發債券，有助於標售參與並減少個別券種間的價格失衡。然而，回購不能消除政府的融資需求，也無法排除決定整體殖利率水準的通膨與財政因素。

當日賣壓的先後順序清楚反映這項區別。公告前，布蘭特原油升破$100，交換市場把聯準會9月16日升息25個基點的機率由前一日60%上調至約62%，2至5年期殖利率因而升至2026年新高。回購條款公布後，長天期債券轉為領跌，10年期殖利率盤中最高觸及4.85%。當下的價格變化是在下修對財政部支持力度的預期，而非市場突然發現新的通膨事件。

10年期殖利率當日漲幅主要來自實質殖利率，損益兩平通膨率也同步上升。實質殖利率上升4個基點，反映市場預期貨幣政策將進一步收緊，以及政府與企業借款人對資本的競爭；損益兩平通膨率上升1.2個基點，則反映能源衝擊持續。過去一個月，10年期名目殖利率累計上升19.6個基點，其中通膨補償增加13.3個基點，實質殖利率增加6.3個基點。

其後標售顯示，只要價格適當，需求仍會回流。財政部增發$390億10年期公債，得標殖利率為4.834%，前次標售則為4.683%。得標水準比標售前殖利率低約1.5個基點，表現比單看殖利率高點所顯示的更強。標售後殖利率自盤中高點回落，但美債全日仍然收低。

即使市場同時面對異常龐大的競爭性供給，公債標售仍吸引買盤。週三有16家美國投資級借款人合計發行$230億債券，週二則有18筆發行；兩日交易筆數為1月5日至6日以來最多。過去八個月中，投資級債發行量有四個月創下同期紀錄，其中包括最近連續三個月；目前發行進度較2020年同期高7.6%。

避險交易可能放大後續殖利率漲勢。投資人已買進選擇權，防範長天期債券進一步下跌，其中一筆顯著部位以30年期殖利率逼近5.7%為目標。當殖利率上升時，承作這類交易的交易商可能必須賣出期貨，或在利率交換中支付固定利率，進一步推動原有走勢。房貸投資人也面臨類似問題：再融資放緩會拉長房貸債券的預期年限，持有人可藉由賣債或在交換中支付固定利率，對沖新增的利率風險。

聯準會減持房貸資產後，更多房貸凸性風險已由民間投資人承擔。這項機制本身不會引發賣壓，卻可能讓通膨、供給或政策預期造成的行情走得更遠。截至9月8日當週，美債客戶已削減直接空頭並轉向中性，使整體淨多頭部位升至去年11月以來最高。市場並非只是在延續擁擠的投機性空頭交易，而是在重新評估承接債券利率風險所需的殖利率。

## 燃料短缺擴大通膨與房市衝擊

原油上漲源於衝突再度升級。美國中央司令部表示，伊朗企圖以彈道飛彈攻擊一艘美國海軍艦艇後，美軍摧毀了伊朗油輪。按現貨市場口徑，布蘭特原油當日收於$101以上，期貨則收在$102.05。全球最大原油進口國中國先前暫停採購，一度有助抑制價格，如今恢復買進，進一步增加需求。

原油供給依然緊俏，但成品油對通膨發出的警訊更直接。伊朗相關敵對行動干擾中東煉油與成品運輸，烏克蘭攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠，也促使莫斯科延長柴油出口限制。運輸成品油所需船舶多於原油，且荷莫茲海峽沒有單一主導機構統籌成品油運輸；一旦航運受限，供應更難維持。

煉油價差因而擴大至紀錄或接近紀錄水準。歐洲柴油期貨較布蘭特原油高約每桶$75，意味稅負與零售利潤前的批發價格接近每桶$175。Vitol執行長Russell Hardy估計，中東與俄羅斯的成品油出口分別每日減少約200萬桶。歐洲駕駛人在加油站支付的汽油與柴油價格，換算後已超過每桶$370。

這項差異說明，央行面對的不只是原油突破$100的醒目數字。英格蘭銀行總裁Andrew Bailey表示，他正密切觀察裂解價差，也就是成品油與原油之間的價差。英格蘭銀行7月曾估計，能源價格上漲將使下半年通膨增加約0.4個百分點，其中汽油與柴油約貢獻0.3個百分點。

歐洲利率市場已反映更強硬的政策回應。交換市場定價顯示，歐洲央行至2027年12月將累計升息約90個基點，相當於三次各25個基點的升息，以及第四次升息60%的機率；英格蘭銀行的定價幅度也大致相同。市場普遍預期歐洲央行將升息25個基點，會議前德國2年期殖利率升至3.08%，創2024年6月以來最高。

部分投資人認為，市場反映的長期升息路徑過度激進。歐洲央行管理委員會成員Joachim Nagel雖表態支持即將到來的升息，卻未支持此後連續行動；Bailey也試圖降低市場對英格蘭銀行立即升息的預期。英國經濟疲弱，加上能源成本尚無充分證據顯示已廣泛滲入歐元區基礎通膨，因此央行仍可採取市場預期的第一步，卻未必需要兌現交換市場反映的每一次升息。

最新油價上漲前，美國家庭財務已顯示高利率正在抑制需求。截至9月4日當週，美國抵押貸款銀行協會統計的30年期房貸合約利率上升6個基點至6.85%，為一年多來最高；自伊朗戰爭開始以來，累計上升約0.75個百分點。5年期浮動利率房貸則反向下降至6.13%。

房貸申請總量在前一週上升0.8%後下降2.7%，市場指數由247.3降至240.6。再融資申請減少6.2%，再融資指數由732.6降至687.3，創2025年5月以來最低；購屋指數則由157.8小幅降至157.5。房貸成本居高不下而需求反應疲弱，在壓低房屋周轉與再融資活動的同時，也延長既有房貸證券的存續期間。

美國其他數據好壞參半，仍不足以蓋過通膨與供給主線。ADP每週就業估計增加12,000人，前值則修正為增加10,000人。截至9月5日當週，Redbook同店銷售較一年前成長8.3%，低於先前的9.6%。就業與零售活動仍在擴張，但並未出現新的全面加速；相較之下，房貸數據更直接顯示利率敏感型需求收縮。

跨資產表現也反映這種平衡。股市下跌，但標普500僅跌0.48%、VIX仍為16.46，與全面拋售並不一致。半導體股上漲0.37%，顯示市場對AI投資週期仍保有一定信心，儘管這項週期也帶來更多債券發行及資本競爭。實質殖利率上升之際，黃金仍受地緣政治風險與美元小幅走弱支撐而上漲。

## 龐大信用債供給順利去化，但投資人更挑剔天期風險

信用市場持續區分基準殖利率上升與企業融資管道惡化。美國投資級債利差當日明顯收窄，週二全球發行量超過$700億，為6月以來最繁忙的一天。信用較強的借款人仍能取得龐大訂單，但個別交易條件顯示，投資人對債券天期、幣別及AI相關借款人反覆融資的區別更加明顯。

戴爾科技籌得$50億，高於原先考慮的約$40億。訂單高峰約達$230億，接近最終發行規模的五倍，也高於今年投資級債交易平均約四倍的水準。四個券次年期介於3至10年，最長一券以美債加110個基點定價，較初步討論水準收窄30個基點。

戴爾將把募集資金用於償還近期票據及一般企業用途，後者可能包括進一步減債。公司10月有$23億債券到期。AI伺服器需求改善其營運表現，讓公司得以在維持BBB評級中段信用狀況的同時進行再融資，而非僅藉這筆交易擴大槓桿。

亞馬遜與Uber則顯示，尋求美元以外選項的美國發行人可以利用歐洲市場的深度。亞馬遜首次發行英鎊債，籌得£42.5億；儘管最終需求由行銷初期逾£120億降至£106.5億，交易規模仍獲提高。四券發行中，最短的3年期券以英國公債加53個基點定價，最長一券則加93個基點。

亞馬遜最長的19年期券接獲訂單最少。其2032年到期債券的需求比年初Alphabet相近年期的英鎊債少£14億，定價利差也更寬。不過，亞馬遜2026年迄今仍已發行近$1,000億等值債券，其中包括一筆$250億美元債，完成公司全年規劃的美元融資。英鎊投資人願意為更多AI支出提供資金，但要求的條件不如先前給予Alphabet的優惠。

Uber首度發行歐元債，透過五個3至20年期固定利率券次籌得€45億。訂單一度超過€210億，最終仍逾€150億。最短一券以中間交換利率加45個基點定價，最長一券則加170個基點。Uber正推動收購Delivery Hero，這筆交易也把原本僅限於美元的融資來源擴展至歐元市場。

週三交易展開前，美國企業2026年已在歐洲以當地貨幣發行€1,490億債券，年度規模僅次於2025年的紀錄。同一天有六家美國企業進入歐洲市場，集中程度前所未見。對擁有歐元收入的企業而言，以歐元借款可能提供較低票息；近期換回美元後的融資成本，也與直接發行美元債相近。更大的優勢是，當超大型科技公司反覆發債使美國市場承壓時，企業可以接觸另一批投資人。

MercadoLibre僅第三度重返全球債市，以美債加130個基點發行$10億2036年到期債券。其既有2033年期債券利差約為100個基點，因此新債定價包含對較長年期與新增供給的讓利。這批債券在Fitch、標普及穆迪均取得投資級的最低一級評等。營收快速成長與流動性充足對信用有利，但物流、客戶開發及放款投資會壓低獲利，並提高融資與資產品質風險。

當日配售順利，並不代表投資人不再區分風險。亞馬遜的英鎊債整體需求充足，但最長券種較乏人問津；Uber的訂單也由高峰明顯下降。MercadoLibre的定價高於既有殖利率曲線，戴爾則在擴大交易規模後仍大幅收窄利差。投資人願意承接新債，但債券天期、重複發行及借款用途日益左右價格。

評級類別之間也出現相同分化。投資級債利差收窄之際，高收益債利差小幅擴大；經配息調整後，HYG與JNK總報酬均下跌約0.18%。硬通貨新興市場債利差小幅收窄，但美債殖利率上升抵銷利差改善，EMB仍下跌0.20%。負報酬主要反映基準利率的存續期間風險，而非信用品質全面惡化。

軟銀的再融資計畫則較接近高收益債市場邊界。公司表示，將於9月15日全數償還一筆$400億過渡性貸款尚餘的$259億。這筆無擔保融資是公司歷來最大的純美元借款，用於投資OpenAI及支付其他成本，原定2027年3月到期。

還款可消除這筆過渡性貸款的到期壓力，卻不會使融資需求消失。軟銀已取得一筆以OpenAI持股擔保的$100億保證金貸款，正尋求另一筆$100億貸款，也在考慮發行$100億至$200億投機級債券，幣別可能包括歐元。公司今年已透過海外與國內債券及保證金貸款，籌得約$250億等值資金。9月15日的現金還款將完成一項負債管理步驟；永久融資的年期、擔保品與成本，才會決定風險究竟轉移了多少，而非消失了多少。

槓桿融資市場同樣活躍。由巴克萊領軍的銀行團，為Lone Star收購ContiTech籌備€24億融資方案，其中包括€19億定期貸款及€5億高收益債。此前，Platinum Equity收購雀巢飲用水事業股權獲得€28億融資，Veritas收購Saber Power Services獲得$12.5億融資，KKR收購Integer Holdings則取得$21億貸款。資金流入也促使至少七家借款人尋求調降既有貸款利差。

這些交易共同說明，企業供給為何會影響政府債券的承接能力，卻不等於信用市場全面破裂。企業提前借款，是因地緣政治波動與通膨可能提高未來融資成本。龐大訂單讓信用最佳的發行人得以改善條件，但每一筆新債仍須與公債標售及其他發行人爭奪投資人的承接額度。美債市場以更高殖利率吸收這場競爭，尚未迫使企業借款人撤退。

## 貝森特施壓日圓，提高日本央行政策門檻

貝森特加大對日本當局的公開施壓，並表示自己的官方職位使他對日本央行及其他日本決策者將採取的行動有異乎尋常的了解，日圓隨後走強。日圓當日升值0.2%，交易價格接近1美元兌153日圓；廣泛美元指標則收在2月以來最低。

新訊息不在於再次進行干預，而在於貝森特以高度確信的口吻，把自己對日圓的支持與日本政策連結起來。日本央行原已傾向在9月18日升息25個基點，市場也大致反映了這一步。貝森特的談話提高了總裁植田和男的政策門檻：除了交付預期中的升息，還必須提出與進一步緊縮相符的指引。

部分投資人已開始考慮升息50個基點或連續升息，前日本央行首席經濟學家龜田制作認為這類預期過度。即使12個月內只升息三次，也會是日本逾30年來最快的緊縮速度。高市早苗政府的財政計畫受惠於較低借款成本，因此也有理由避免突然展開連續升息。

這種不對稱性使會議結果帶有風險。日圓升值可降低進口能源成本，有助日本央行推動政策正常化，卻也可能減少積極緊縮的必要。若央行僅例行升息25個基點並提出審慎指引，可能使那些把貝森特介入解讀為協調政策路徑證據的投資人失望；若政策明顯加速，則可能強化日圓融資套利交易的平倉。

官方實際干預規模也提供重要背景。美國在7月行動中的投入估計僅約$5億，遠低於貝森特公開展示的$50億至$100億方案，日本則投入約$960億。後續口頭施壓推動日圓突破操作後立即觸及的水準；避險基金也利用選擇權押注日圓升破150，部分較長天期結構的目標甚至接近140。

日圓升值已促使投資人另覓亞洲低成本融資貨幣。過去三個月，以離岸人民幣融資並投資八種新興市場貨幣的一籃子策略報酬為1.5%，類似的日圓融資策略則虧損1%。9月前八日，美元兌離岸人民幣賣權的日均交易量較8月平均增加逾60%；隨著人民幣融資需求上升，市場對沖人民幣升值的需求也在增加。

相較美國、日本與英國殖利率上升，中國利率較低且更穩定。中國人民銀行也透過每日中間價表明，不希望人民幣大幅升值。不過，人民幣流動性較低且不能自由兌換，限制其完全取代日圓的能力；較長天期的離岸人民幣融資尤其缺乏深度。

北京同時準備開闢另一條管道，讓境內資金投資離岸債券。中國計畫允許規模達$5,680億的全國社會保障基金，透過債券通南向通買債，無須另行申請境外投資額度。基金管理機構正透過外部資產管理人籌備點心債投資計畫。

這項改變將為已連續14個月錄得離岸債券淨買進的南向通，引進一個大型潛在投資人。7月中國境內機構透過該管道增持估計496億元人民幣，為六個月最多。2026年點心債年度發行量已達約8,300億元人民幣，較一年前增加逾30%；南向通額度則預定提高至8,000億元人民幣。

吸引力部分來自殖利率。國家電網近期發行票息2.18%的10年期離岸人民幣債，較隔週發行的同天期境內債高約20個基點。截至2025年底，中國社保基金的境外投資為5,800億元人民幣，占資產15.23%。香港債市准入更便利，可讓更多境內儲蓄流向這項離岸溢酬；與此同時，人民幣本身也日益受到融資交易關注。

## 政策利率按兵不動與資產負債表風險凸顯區域分歧

波蘭連續第六個月把基準利率維持在3.75%，符合34名經濟學家一致預測。8月通膨升至3.4%，創14個月新高，接近央行2.5%目標加減1個百分點區間的上緣。經濟成長加快、燃料成本上升，已使央行總裁Adam Glapinski在7月提及的降息不再是近期選項。

決策公布後，波蘭茲羅提變動不大。貨幣政策委員會表示，後續行動將取決於數據、商品價格及全球環境。各家預測差異很大：Bank Pekao認為利率將維持不變至2027年底，Bank Pocztowy預期下一次降息要到該年下半年，法國農業信貸銀行則預測2026年第4季將升息25個基點。Glapinski的記者會將決定，此次按兵不動代表長期暫停，還是轉向緊縮的過渡期。

智利也把利率維持在4.5%，但最新預測顯示，政策組合遠比利率不變所呈現的更棘手。央行第三度下修2026年成長預測，由1%至1.75%降至0.25%至0.75%，2027年預測則維持2%至3%。就在去年12月，央行對2026年的成長預測仍為2%至3%。

7月經濟活動下降1.7%，為2022年以來最大單月跌幅，礦業、商業與服務業均轉弱。與此同時，8月通膨較一年前升至4.1%，月增0.6%，是預測中位數的兩倍，主因食品、交通與燃料成本上漲。央行一致決定維持利率，保留了應對兩面風險的彈性：一面是國內經濟持續疲弱，另一面是外部能源衝擊；若聯準會升息，後者還可能推高美元。

墨西哥8月通膨較為溫和。整體通膨由3.12%升至3.26%，低於3.30%的預測；核心通膨則由3.95%降至3.88%，也低於3.92%的估計。兩者仍處於墨西哥央行3%目標加減1個百分點的區間內，但服務價格壓力持續、勞動成本上升及中東衝突，都使央行沒有太大理由推翻將政策利率維持在6.5%的決定。

墨西哥預算案提出了更直接的主權信用問題。政府計畫在2027年把對墨西哥石油公司的支援削減近70%，編列810億披索、即$48億，協助支付債務。墨西哥石油公司明年約有$50億債務到期；若不計政府支援，官員預測公司將有140億披索財務盈餘。

支援縮減前，政府已為公司2026年債務投入$140億資本，並以一筆$100億操作清償今年到期債務。墨西哥石油公司提議的2027年預算增加2%至5,270億披索，其中基礎建設支出增至約2,360億披索，接近原先四倍。墨西哥仍預期明年財政赤字占GDP 3.9%，雖低於今年的4.1%，但社會與基礎建設支出擴張使赤字仍處高檔。

這項計畫假設，一家成熟油田產量下滑、煉油業務長期虧損的公司，能在大舉投資之際顯著提高自給能力。總統Claudia Sheinbaum上任頭兩年已提供逾$500億支援，其前任政府另提供約$800億。因此，2027年撥款減少，是對營運改善、民間合作及市場融資能力的考驗，並不代表主權與公司信用之間的連結已經終止。

華晨能源更直接反映債權人風險仍未解決。先前展延的到期日將於12月屆滿，這家中國民營發電商正尋求把美元與人民幣債券再延長6年。擬議票息第一年由6%起，每年增加0.5個百分點，至第六年升至8.5%。

爭議核心是華晨每年應償還多少本金。方案仍可能調整；若公司清償指定比例的本金，則可降低利息成本。華晨約有$6.27億美元債券流通在外；2021年完成法院批准的重整時，其境內債券價值約為20億元人民幣。當時協議把到期日延後5年，卻未能使資產負債表充分復原，因而仍須再次協商。

並非所有去槓桿都仰賴展期或政府支援。Dangote Petroleum Refinery截至6月底的有擔保債務由去年12月的$62.4億降至$56.7億。產量增加，加上戰爭相關供應中斷推升銷售，公司上半年獲利$18.2億，前一年同期則虧損$2.821億。淨負債降至稅息折舊及攤銷前盈餘的0.27倍。

Dangote計畫自9月14日起辦理首次公開發行，籌資$16億；視需求與主管機關批准情況，金額可能提高至約$21億。公司也計畫投入$143億，在2030年前把煉油產能提高一倍，但表示這筆支出並非眼前的資金需求。Dangote與墨西哥石油公司及華晨的差別，在於目前的現金創造能力：油品價格上漲提高Dangote的償債能力，卻同時惡化能源進口國的通膨與財政壓力。

歐洲銀行融資則面臨一項逐步推進的擔保品制度變化。歐洲央行計畫把氣候風險因子由公司債擴大至信用債權；後者占歐元體系質押擔保品近30%。自2027年底起，受影響資產初期將依轉型風險，額外適用最高5%的折價率。

銀行及產業團體反對歐洲央行只公布概括方法，不披露個別評分或其組成。目前再融資貸款僅約€260億，可用擔保品則有€1.59兆，因此即時流動性影響有限。真正重要的是未來的壓力情境：若規模大得多的資產類別適用透明度較低的折價率，可能改變銀行拿哪些貸款作為擔保，以及如何為轉型風險較高的借款人定價。

聯準會則在考慮另一項制度變革。至少六名地區聯準銀行總裁，包括克里夫蘭聯準銀行的Beth Hammack、堪薩斯城聯準銀行的Jeffrey Schmid及費城聯準銀行的Anna Paulson，都表示願意考慮減少每年例行政策會議的次數。主席Kevin Warsh提議舉行六次利率決策會議，另安排兩次會議討論重大經濟議題；自1981年以來，聯準會每年均召開八次例會。

目前尚未作成決定，官員希望分析會議次數減少將如何影響預測、記者會及央行溝通策略。五個外部工作小組預計在年底前後提出建議。這項提案不會改變眼前的9月決策，但日後可能把政策事件風險集中在更少日期，並改變經濟預測發布的節奏。

## 後市意義

下一個美國交易日將同時迎來首次擴大回購、長天期公債供給及重要通膨數據。財政部9月10日將回購10至20年期債券，初步上限為$60億。公告本身已推高殖利率，最終承作金額與買進分布將顯示這項計畫能提供多少流動性支持。隨後還有30年期公債標售，前次得標殖利率為5.216%。評估需求時應檢視可取得的標售指標，而非只看殖利率。

8月生產者物價也將在同日公布。整體PPI預計在7月零成長後月增0.4%，核心PPI則預計由0.2%加速至0.3%。整體年增率預計由4.7%升至5.3%，核心通膨由4.2%升至4.6%。扣除食品、能源與貿易的指標預計月增0.3%，年增率則由4.7%放緩至4.4%。

初領失業救濟金人數預計約為20.5萬人，前值20.6萬人；續領人數預計約178萬人，前值177.9萬人。ADP每週就業增加12,000人，未動搖最新非農就業數據所反映的情況；在房貸與家庭借款成本上升之際，失業救濟申請能更直接檢驗裁員是否仍維持低檔。

市場普遍預期歐洲央行將升息25個基點，交換市場還反映了一條遠為漫長的緊縮路徑，因此政策指引比眼前這一步更重要。即使數名投資人認為，廣泛通膨壓力的證據不足以支持這種升息節奏，市場仍定價至2027年底將累計升息約90個基點。儘管丹麥克朗疲弱，且丹麥自6月以來已干預63億克朗，市場仍預期丹麥央行將跟隨歐洲央行升息，而非自行收緊政策。

美國CPI將於9月11日公布。整體通膨預計月增0.4%，年增率維持3.4%；核心通膨預計月增0.2%，年增率則由2.5%降至2.4%。若核心結果溫和，聯準會仍可把嚴重燃料衝擊與更廣泛的通膨持續性分開處理。若能源以外價格加速，將強化9月15日至16日會議採取行動的理由；交換市場目前認為升息25個基點的機率約為62%。

9月11日稍晚公布的密西根大學9月初值，將補充家庭信心與通膨預期訊息。消費者信心預計接近51，前值51.7；此前1年期通膨預期為4%，5年期為3.3%。若高油價開始改變長期通膨預期，而非僅削弱購買力，這些指標持續偏高的重要性將進一步上升。

軟銀預定於9月15日還款，將檢驗過渡性貸款再融資是否如公告推進。償還$259億餘額可消除近期到期壓力，但投資人仍須取得可能發行的$100億至$200億債券及其他永久融資條件，才能評估交易後的槓桿、擔保品與到期結構。

9月16日聯準會決策仍是美國最關鍵的政策事件。油價、PPI與CPI將決定，就業強勁是否伴隨足以促成三年來首次升息的通膨壓力。經濟預測將顯示，官員把升息視為一次性回應，還是進一步緊縮的起點；市場已反映至2027年中至少升息兩次。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries fell across the curve as a fresh surge in energy prices met a Treasury buyback plan that proved too small to satisfy the market’s most aggressive expectations. The 10-year yield rose 5.2 basis points to 4.842%, its highest since 2023, while the 5-year climbed 5.3 basis points to 4.617%. The 2-year increased 3.7 basis points to 4.432%, and the 30-year added 4.4 basis points to 5.29%.

The selloff began with another escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict and accelerated after the Treasury set a $6 billion maximum for its Sept. 10 purchase of outstanding 10- to 20-year securities. That was three times the previously scheduled amount but below speculation that an individual operation could reach $8 billion to $10 billion. Shorter maturities had led the initial rise in yields as oil strengthened expectations for Federal Reserve tightening; long maturities took over after the buyback announcement disappointed.

The resulting curve move was modestly steeper rather than the flattening seen during the previous session’s oil shock. The 2s10s spread widened 1.5 basis points to 41 basis points, and 2s30s increased 0.7 basis point to 85.8. The 10-year real yield rose 4 basis points to 2.455%, while the 10-year breakeven gained 1.2 basis points to 2.387%. Investors demanded more real compensation as they confronted the combination of less official support than anticipated, heavy government and corporate financing, and a stronger prospective policy response; inflation compensation also rose as the energy shock intensified.

A well-received $39 billion 10-year auction interrupted but did not reverse the decline. The notes were awarded at 4.834%, the highest auction yield since 2007 but about 1.5 basis points below the yield in pre-auction trading, indicating demand at the elevated level. Treasuries pared their losses after the sale and still ended broadly 3 to 5 basis points cheaper. The auction showed that buyers would absorb duration at current yields, while the earlier reaction to the buyback showed that private demand was not prepared to grant Treasury a lower clearing rate merely because it expanded purchases of older debt.

Energy supplied the other side of the pressure. Brent futures rose 4.22% to $102.05 and WTI gained 4.28% to $97.01 after U.S. forces destroyed Iranian tankers and China resumed crude purchases. More important for central banks, the squeeze in refined fuels was substantially more severe than the headline crude move. European diesel futures traded at a premium of about $75 a barrel over Brent, compared with roughly $21 at the start of the year, as conflict in the Middle East and attacks on Russian refineries removed an estimated 4 million barrels a day of refined-product exports.

The risk response remained controlled rather than disorderly. The S&P 500 fell 0.48%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.29%, and the VIX rose 4.71% to 16.46. The Dollar Index edged 0.06% lower to 98.783, partly because the yen strengthened after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent intensified pressure for tighter Japanese policy. Gold futures rose 1.15% to $4,444.60. U.S. investment-grade spreads tightened clearly despite the Treasury selloff and a large slate of new bonds; high-yield spreads widened modestly, while hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly.

The session therefore combined two different tests of bond-market capacity. Treasury’s intervention did less than investors hoped to contain long-term yields, but the government auction and corporate primary market still attracted substantial demand at higher all-in borrowing costs. The result was not a funding seizure. It was a market insisting on greater compensation while inflation, monetary policy, fiscal supply and technology-related capital spending compete for the same duration capacity.

## Buyback Disappointment Leaves Treasury Yields at Multiyear Highs

Treasury had already promised to at least double the $2 billion maximum for several long-dated buybacks after an abrupt August revision to its schedule. The first specific increase took the Sept. 10 operation in the 10- to 20-year sector to as much as $6 billion. Six other nominal buybacks in the 10- to 30-year range through Nov. 5 will have maximums of at least $4 billion, with the precise size normally announced shortly before each operation.

Those figures were large relative to the existing program but small relative to the expectations encouraged by Bessent’s public campaign to restrain long-term borrowing costs. Strategists had contemplated individual purchases as high as $10 billion after the Treasury secretary described the expansion as an effort to cool a bond-market “fever.” The gap between those expectations and the announced amount mattered more than the mechanical reduction in outstanding off-the-run securities.

The $6 billion is also stated at par value. Because many of the eligible older bonds trade below face value, the cash Treasury will deploy can be smaller than the headline maximum. The department usually fills its announced maximum in long-dated nominal operations, but it is not obligated to do so. Its final announcement on the day of the operation can supersede the preliminary size.

The market response clarified what buybacks can and cannot accomplish. They can improve liquidity in less-traded securities and allow dealers or investors to replace older holdings with newly issued debt. That may support auction participation and reduce isolated dislocations between securities. They do not eliminate the government’s financing requirement or the inflation and fiscal forces determining the broader level of yields.

The sequence of the selloff made that distinction visible. Before the announcement, 2- to 5-year yields reached new highs for 2026 as Brent moved above $100 and swaps raised the probability of a quarter-point Fed increase on Sept. 16 to about 62%, from 60% the day before. After the buyback terms were released, longer maturities led the decline, and the 10-year yield traded as high as 4.85%. Investors were marking down anticipated Treasury support rather than discovering a new inflation event at that moment.

The real-yield increase accounted for most of the day’s 10-year move, but breakevens did not remain passive. The 4-basis-point rise in the real yield was consistent with expectations for greater monetary restraint and the competition for capital from public and corporate borrowers. The 1.2-basis-point increase in breakevens reflected the continuing energy impulse. Over the past month, the 10-year nominal yield has risen 19.6 basis points, including a 13.3-basis-point increase in inflation compensation and a 6.3-basis-point rise in the real yield.

The auction later demonstrated that price could still restore demand. Treasury increased the outstanding 10-year issue by $39 billion, awarding it at 4.834%, compared with 4.683% at the previous auction. The stop was about 1.5 basis points through the pre-sale yield, a stronger result than the headline level alone would suggest. Yields retreated from their intraday highs afterward, although the market remained lower on the session.

That demand arrived despite exceptionally heavy competing supply. Sixteen U.S. investment-grade borrowers sold a combined $23 billion on Wednesday, following 18 offerings on Tuesday. The two-day deal count was the largest since Jan. 5-6. Investment-grade volume has set monthly records in four of the past eight months, including the last three, and was running 7.6% above the comparable 2020 pace.

Hedging flows risk amplifying subsequent rises. Investors have bought options against a further long-end selloff, including a notable position targeting a 30-year yield near 5.7%. Dealers facing those trades may need to sell futures or pay fixed rates in swaps as yields rise, adding momentum to the underlying move. Mortgage investors face a related problem: as refinancing slows, expected mortgage-bond maturities lengthen, and holders can hedge the added duration by selling bonds or paying fixed in swaps.

More of that mortgage convexity exposure now sits with private investors after the Federal Reserve reduced its mortgage holdings. The mechanism does not initiate a selloff by itself, but it can make a move driven by inflation, supply or policy expectations travel farther. Treasury clients had already reduced outright short positions in the week through Sept. 8 and shifted toward neutral, leaving aggregate net-long positioning at its highest since November. The market was therefore not simply extending a crowded speculative short; it was repricing the yield required to absorb duration.

## Fuel Scarcity Broadens the Inflation and Housing Shock

The oil advance followed another escalation in the conflict. U.S. Central Command said American forces destroyed Iranian tankers after attempted ballistic-missile attacks on a U.S. Navy vessel. Brent settled above $101 in the cash-market account of the session, while the futures series finished at $102.05. Renewed Chinese buying added demand after a hiatus by the world’s largest crude importer had previously helped restrain prices.

The crude market remained tight, but refined fuels carried the more direct inflation warning. Iranian hostilities have disrupted Middle Eastern refining and product shipments, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries prompted Moscow to extend restrictions on diesel exports. Petroleum products require more vessels than crude and lack a single dominant organizer of transit through the Strait of Hormuz, making their movements harder to sustain when shipping is constrained.

The result was a record or near-record widening in processing margins. European diesel futures traded about $75 above Brent, implying a wholesale price near $175 a barrel, before taxes and retail margins. Vitol Chief Executive Russell Hardy estimated that roughly 2 million barrels a day of refined-product exports had been lost from the Middle East and another 2 million from Russia. European motorists were paying the equivalent of more than $370 a barrel for gasoline and diesel at the pump.

That distinction helps explain why central banks were responding to more than the $100 crude headline. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said he was watching crack spreads—the difference between finished-fuel and crude prices—particularly closely. The BOE had estimated in July that higher energy prices would add about 0.4 percentage point to inflation in the second half of the year, with gasoline and diesel contributing roughly 0.3 point.

The European rates market priced a more forceful response. Swaps implied around 90 basis points of European Central Bank tightening through December 2027, equivalent to three quarter-point increases and a 60% probability of a fourth. Roughly the same amount was priced for the Bank of England. Two-year German yields reached 3.08%, their highest since June 2024, ahead of an ECB meeting at which a 25-basis-point increase was widely expected.

Several investors regarded the longer tightening path as excessive. ECB Governing Council member Joachim Nagel had signaled support for the imminent increase without endorsing repeated action beyond it, while Bailey had sought to reduce expectations for an immediate BOE move. The weak UK economy and limited evidence that energy costs had spread broadly into underlying euro-area inflation left room for the expected first step without validating every increase embedded in swaps.

U.S. household finance showed that higher rates were already exerting restraint before the latest oil move. The Mortgage Bankers Association’s contract rate on a 30-year mortgage rose 6 basis points to 6.85% in the week through Sept. 4, its highest in more than a year and up about three-quarters of a percentage point since the Iran war began. The 5-year adjustable rate moved in the opposite direction, declining to 6.13%.

Total mortgage applications fell 2.7% after rising 0.8% the previous week. The market index dropped to 240.6 from 247.3. Refinancing applications fell 6.2%, taking the refinance index to 687.3 from 732.6 and its lowest level since May 2025. The purchase index slipped to 157.5 from 157.8. The weak response to elevated mortgage costs increases the duration of existing mortgage securities even as it reduces housing turnover and refinancing activity.

Other U.S. releases were mixed and did not outweigh the inflation and supply story. ADP’s weekly employment estimate showed an increase of 12,000, compared with a revised 10,000 previously. Redbook same-store sales rose 8.3% from a year earlier in the week through Sept. 5, slowing from 9.6%. The combination suggested continued employment and retail activity without a fresh broad acceleration, while the mortgage figures showed a more direct contraction in rate-sensitive demand.

The cross-asset outcome reflected that balance. Equities declined, but the 0.48% S&P 500 loss and a VIX level of 16.46 were inconsistent with a generalized liquidation. Semiconductor shares rose 0.37%, preserving some of the market’s confidence in the AI investment cycle even as that cycle contributed to bond issuance and competition for capital. Gold advanced despite the rise in real yields, supported by geopolitical risk and a slightly weaker dollar.

## Heavy Credit Supply Clears, but Duration Demand Turns Selective

Credit markets continued to distinguish higher benchmark yields from deteriorating corporate access. U.S. investment-grade spreads tightened clearly on the day, and Tuesday’s global issuance of more than $70 billion was the busiest session since June. Stronger borrowers still found large order books, although the terms of individual transactions showed greater discrimination over duration, currency and repeated AI-related financing.

Dell Technologies raised $5 billion, exceeding the roughly $4 billion initially contemplated. Orders reached about $23 billion at their peak, almost five times the final size and above the approximately four-times average for investment-grade transactions this year. The four tranches ranged from 3 to 10 years, and the longest bond priced 110 basis points over Treasuries, 30 basis points tighter than the initial discussion.

Dell will use the proceeds to repay near-term notes and for general corporate purposes that may include additional debt reduction. It has $2.3 billion of bonds maturing in October. AI-server demand has strengthened its operating results, allowing the company to refinance while preserving a mid-BBB credit profile rather than using the transaction solely to expand leverage.

Amazon and Uber demonstrated the depth of European markets for U.S. issuers seeking alternatives to dollars. Amazon raised £4.25 billion in its debut sterling offering and increased the deal’s size even as final demand declined to £10.65 billion from more than £12 billion earlier in marketing. The four-part sale priced the shortest 3-year tranche 53 basis points over gilts and the longest at 93 basis points.

The longest Amazon tranche, at 19 years, attracted the fewest orders. Its 2032 bond received £1.4 billion less demand and priced at a wider spread than the comparable maturity in Alphabet’s sterling transaction earlier in the year. Amazon has nevertheless sold the equivalent of nearly $100 billion of bonds in 2026, including a $25 billion dollar offering that completed its planned dollar funding for the year. Sterling investors were willing to finance more of the company’s AI spending, but they required less aggressive terms than those granted to Alphabet.

Uber raised €4.5 billion from its first euro transaction, selling five fixed-rate tranches from 3 to 20 years. Final orders exceeded €15 billion after peaking above €21 billion. The shortest bond priced 45 basis points over mid-swaps and the longest at 170 basis points. The transaction diversified a funding base previously confined to dollars while Uber pursued its acquisition of Delivery Hero.

Before Wednesday’s transactions, U.S.-domiciled companies had already issued €149 billion in European currencies during 2026, the second-highest annual total after the 2025 record. Six American companies approached European markets in a single day, an unprecedented concentration. Euro borrowing can offer cheaper coupons to companies with euro revenues, while swapped dollar costs have recently been close to direct dollar funding. The larger advantage is access to another investor base when repeated hyperscaler sales are straining the U.S. market.

MercadoLibre returned to global debt for only the third time, selling $1 billion of notes due in 2036 at 130 basis points over Treasuries. Its existing 2033 notes traded near a 100-basis-point spread, so the new deal incorporated a concession for maturity and supply. The bonds carry the lowest investment-grade ratings at Fitch, S&P and Moody’s. Rapid revenue growth and strong liquidity support the credit, while investment in logistics, customer acquisition and lending reduces profitability and raises funding and asset-quality risks.

The day’s placement strength therefore did not eliminate differentiation. Amazon found ample sterling demand but weaker appetite for its longest maturity. Uber’s order book declined materially from its peak. MercadoLibre paid above its existing curve, while Dell tightened sharply after enlarging its deal. Investors were prepared to absorb new bonds, but duration, repeated issuance and the purpose of borrowing increasingly determined the price.

That distinction also appeared between rating classes. High-yield spreads widened modestly even as investment-grade spreads tightened, and the distribution-adjusted total returns of HYG and JNK declined about 0.18%. Hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened modestly, although EMB lost 0.20% as higher Treasury yields offset the spread improvement. Benchmark-rate duration, rather than a uniform deterioration in credit quality, accounted for much of the negative return.

SoftBank’s refinancing plan sits closer to the high-yield boundary. The company said it will repay the entire $25.9 billion outstanding balance of a $40 billion bridge loan on Sept. 15. The unsecured facility, its largest dollar-only borrowing, financed its OpenAI investment and other costs and was due to mature in March 2027.

Repayment removes the bridge maturity but does not eliminate the financing need. SoftBank has secured a $10 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake, is seeking another $10 billion loan, and is considering a $10 billion to $20 billion speculative-grade bond sale that could include euros. It has already raised the equivalent of about $25 billion this year through offshore and domestic bonds and a margin loan. The Sept. 15 cash payment will complete one liability-management step; the maturity, collateral and cost of the permanent financing will determine how much risk has actually moved rather than disappeared.

Leveraged finance remained active as well. A Barclays-led group prepared a €2.4 billion package for Lone Star’s acquisition of ContiTech, including a €1.9 billion term loan and €500 million high-yield bond. The deal followed a €2.8 billion financing for Platinum Equity’s purchase of a stake in Nestlé’s water business, a $1.25 billion package for Veritas’s acquisition of Saber Power Services and a $2.1 billion loan for KKR’s purchase of Integer Holdings. Fund inflows also encouraged at least seven borrowers to seek lower margins on existing loans.

Together, those transactions show why corporate supply is relevant to government duration without implying a broad credit break. Companies are advancing borrowing because geopolitical volatility and inflation could raise future costs. Strong order books allow the best credits to tighten terms, but every new bond still competes with Treasury auctions and other issuers for balance-sheet capacity. The Treasury market absorbed that competition at higher yields rather than forcing corporate borrowers to retreat.

## Bessent’s Yen Campaign Raises the Bar for the BOJ

The yen strengthened after Bessent escalated his public pressure campaign, saying his official position gave him unusual insight into what the Bank of Japan and other Japanese policymakers would do. The currency gained 0.2% on the day and traded near 153 per dollar, while the broad U.S. dollar gauge finished at its weakest level since February.

The immediate novelty was not another intervention but the confidence with which Bessent linked his support for the currency to Japanese policy. The BOJ was already leaning toward a 25-basis-point increase on Sept. 18, and markets had largely priced that step. His remarks increased the burden on Governor Kazuo Ueda to provide guidance consistent with further tightening rather than merely deliver the expected move.

Some investors had begun considering a 50-basis-point increase or consecutive hikes, expectations former BOJ chief economist Seisaku Kameda described as excessive. Three increases within 12 months would already be Japan’s fastest tightening in more than three decades. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government also has reason to avoid an abrupt sequence because its fiscal program benefits from lower borrowing costs.

The asymmetry creates a risk around the meeting. A stronger yen reduces imported energy costs and supports the BOJ’s normalization effort, but it can also diminish the need for aggressive tightening. A routine quarter-point increase accompanied by cautious guidance could therefore disappoint a market that has interpreted Bessent’s intervention as evidence of a coordinated policy path. A sharper acceleration could intensify the closing of yen-funded carry trades.

The scale of the official intervention adds perspective. The U.S. contribution to the July operation was estimated at about $500 million, far below the $5 billion to $10 billion plan Bessent displayed publicly. Japan spent about $96 billion. Subsequent verbal pressure helped take the yen beyond levels reached immediately after the operation, and hedge funds were using options to target gains through 150 and, in some longer-dated structures, toward 140.

Yen appreciation has already encouraged investors to look for another low-cost Asian funding currency. An offshore-yuan-funded basket of eight emerging-market currencies returned 1.5% over the past three months, compared with a 1% loss for a comparable yen-funded strategy. Daily average trading in dollar-offshore-yuan put options rose more than 60% during the first eight days of September from the August average, indicating greater demand for protection against yuan appreciation as funding interest increased.

China’s lower and more stable rates contrast with rising yields in the U.S., Japan and the UK. The People’s Bank of China has also signaled through its daily reference rate that it resists substantial yuan appreciation. The currency remains less liquid and is not freely convertible, limiting its ability to replace the yen completely. Longer-dated offshore yuan borrowing is particularly shallow.

Beijing was simultaneously preparing another channel for domestic capital to enter offshore bonds. China plans to allow its $568 billion National Social Security Fund to buy through Southbound Bond Connect without applying separately for overseas investment quotas. The fund manager was preparing dim sum bond plans through external asset managers.

The change would add a large potential investor to a program already recording 14 consecutive months of net offshore bond purchases. Mainland institutions added an estimated 49.6 billion yuan through the channel in July, the most in six months. Annual dim sum issuance has reached about 830 billion yuan in 2026, more than 30% above a year earlier, while the Southbound quota is due to rise to 800 billion yuan.

The attraction is partly yield. State Grid recently sold a 10-year offshore yuan bond with a 2.18% coupon, about 20 basis points above the same-tenor onshore bond it issued the following week. China’s social security fund had 580 billion yuan of overseas investments at the end of 2025, equal to 15.23% of assets. Easier access to Hong Kong debt can redirect more domestic savings toward that offshore premium even as the yuan itself becomes a more closely watched funding currency.

## Policy Holds and Balance-Sheet Risks Expose Regional Fault Lines

Poland kept its benchmark rate at 3.75% for a sixth month, matching the unanimous forecast of 34 economists. Inflation reached a 14-month high of 3.4% in August, close to the top of the central bank’s 2.5% target plus or minus 1 percentage point. Faster growth and higher fuel costs had already removed the rate cut Governor Adam Glapinski suggested in July from immediate consideration.

The zloty was little changed after the decision. The Monetary Policy Council said future action would depend on data, commodity prices and the global environment. Forecasts diverged widely: Bank Pekao expected rates to remain unchanged through the end of 2027, Bank Pocztowy saw the next reduction in the second half of that year, while Credit Agricole anticipated a quarter-point increase in the fourth quarter of 2026. Glapinski’s press conference will determine whether the hold represents a long pause or a transition toward tightening.

Chile also held at 4.5%, but its updated projections showed a more difficult policy mix than the unchanged rate conveyed. The central bank cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.25%-0.75% from 1%-1.75%, its third downgrade, while leaving the 2027 range at 2%-3%. As recently as December, it had projected 2%-3% growth for 2026.

Economic activity fell 1.7% in July, the largest monthly decline since 2022, with mining, commerce and services all weaker. At the same time, August inflation accelerated to 4.1% from a year earlier and 0.6% on the month, twice the median forecast, as food, transportation and fuel costs rose. The unanimous rate hold preserved flexibility between persistent domestic weakness and an external energy shock that could also strengthen the dollar if the Fed tightens.

Mexico’s August inflation figures were less severe. Headline inflation increased to 3.26% from 3.12%, below the 3.30% forecast. Core inflation slowed to 3.88% from 3.95%, also below the 3.92% estimate. Both remained within Banxico’s 3% target range of plus or minus 1 percentage point, but persistent services pressure, rising labor costs and the Middle East conflict left little reason to reverse the bank’s decision to keep its policy rate at 6.5%.

Mexico’s budget presented a more direct sovereign-credit question. The government plans to reduce support for Pemex by almost 70% in 2027, allocating 81 billion pesos, or $4.8 billion, to help cover debt payments. Pemex has about $5 billion of maturities next year. Excluding government support, officials forecast a 14 billion-peso financial surplus at the company.

The reduction follows $14 billion of capital injections for 2026 obligations and a $10 billion operation to retire this year’s maturities. Pemex’s proposed 2027 budget rises 2% to 527 billion pesos, including an almost fourfold increase in infrastructure spending to about 236 billion pesos. Mexico still expects a fiscal deficit of 3.9% of GDP next year, narrower than 4.1% this year but elevated as social and infrastructure spending expands.

The plan assumes that a company with declining mature-field production and historically loss-making refining operations can become much more self-sufficient while investing heavily. President Claudia Sheinbaum has provided more than $50 billion of support during her first two years, on top of roughly $80 billion under her predecessor. The smaller 2027 allocation is therefore a test of operating improvement, private partnerships and market access rather than evidence that the sovereign-credit linkage has ended.

Huachen Energy provided a more explicit case of unresolved creditor risk. The Chinese private power producer is seeking to extend its dollar- and yuan-denominated bonds by another 6 years as an earlier maturity extension expires in December. The proposed coupon would begin at 6% in the first year and rise by 0.5 percentage point annually to 8.5% in the sixth.

The central disagreement is the amount of principal Huachen would repay each year. The proposal remains subject to change and would allow lower interest costs if the company retires a specified portion of principal. Huachen has about $627 million of dollar notes outstanding; its onshore bonds were worth roughly 2 billion yuan when it completed a court-approved restructuring in 2021. That agreement postponed maturities by 5 years but did not generate enough balance-sheet recovery to avoid another negotiation.

Not all deleveraging depended on extensions or sovereign support. Dangote Petroleum Refinery reduced secured debt to $5.67 billion at the end of June from $6.24 billion in December. It reported a $1.82 billion first-half profit, compared with a $282.1 million loss a year earlier, as production increased and war-related supply disruptions lifted sales. Net debt fell to 0.27 times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization.

Dangote plans to raise $1.6 billion in an initial public offering beginning Sept. 14, with the amount potentially increasing to about $2.1 billion subject to demand and regulatory approval. It also plans a $14.3 billion expansion to double refining capacity by 2030, although the company said that spending was not an immediate funding requirement. The contrast with Pemex and Huachen is one of current cash generation: higher oil and fuel prices improved Dangote’s capacity to repay debt even as they worsened inflation and fiscal pressures for energy importers.

European bank funding faces a slower-moving collateral change. The ECB plans to extend a climate-risk factor from corporate bonds to credit claims, which represent close to 30% of collateral pledged in the Eurosystem. From the end of 2027, affected assets may receive an additional haircut of as much as 5% based initially on transition risk.

Banks and industry groups have objected that the ECB will disclose only the broad methodology rather than individual scores or their components. Refinancing lending is currently only about €26 billion against €1.59 trillion of available collateral, so the immediate liquidity impact is limited. The importance lies in future stressed conditions: a less transparent haircut on a much larger asset class could alter which loans banks pledge and how they price borrowers with high transition exposure.

The Fed was considering a separate institutional change. At least six regional presidents, including Cleveland’s Beth Hammack, Kansas City’s Jeffrey Schmid and Philadelphia’s Anna Paulson, expressed openness to reducing the annual number of scheduled policy meetings. Chair Kevin Warsh proposed six rate-setting meetings, with two additional sessions devoted to substantive economic topics, compared with the eight-meeting calendar used since 1981.

No decision has been taken, and officials want analysis of how fewer meetings would affect forecasts, press conferences and the central bank’s communication strategy. Five outside task forces are expected to make recommendations near year-end. The proposal does not alter the immediate September decision, but it could eventually concentrate policy-event risk into fewer dates and change the cadence at which economic projections are released.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. session combines the first enlarged buyback, long-duration supply and major inflation data. Treasury’s Sept. 10 operation will target 10- to 20-year securities with a preliminary maximum of $6 billion. The accepted amount and the distribution of purchases will show how much liquidity support the program provides after the announcement itself lifted yields. A 30-year auction follows, with the previous sale having cleared at 5.216%. Demand will be judged against the available auction metrics, not the yield in isolation.

August producer prices are due the same day. Headline PPI is expected to rise 0.4% after no change in July, while core PPI is expected to increase 0.3% after 0.2%. The annual headline rate is expected to accelerate to 5.3% from 4.7%, and core inflation to 4.6% from 4.2%. The measure excluding food, energy and trade is forecast to rise 0.3% on the month and slow to 4.4% annually from 4.7%.

Initial jobless claims are expected near 205,000 after 206,000, with continuing claims around 1.78 million after 1.779 million. The weekly ADP gain of 12,000 did not challenge the latest payroll evidence, but claims will provide a cleaner test of whether low layoffs persist while mortgage and household borrowing costs rise.

The ECB decision arrives against expectations for a 25-basis-point increase and a much longer tightening path embedded in swaps. The immediate move is broadly anticipated. Guidance matters because markets price about 90 basis points of increases through the end of 2027 even as several investors see insufficient evidence of broad inflation pressure to justify that sequence. Denmark’s central bank is expected to match an ECB increase rather than tighten independently, despite a weak krone and 6.3 billion kroner of intervention since June.

U.S. CPI follows on Sept. 11. Headline inflation is expected to rise 0.4% on the month and remain at 3.4% annually. Core inflation is expected at 0.2% monthly and 2.4% from a year earlier, down from 2.5%. A contained core result would leave the Fed to distinguish a severe fuel shock from broader inflation persistence. Acceleration outside energy would reinforce the case for action at the Sept. 15-16 meeting, for which swaps assign roughly a 62% probability of a quarter-point increase.

Preliminary September University of Michigan data later on Sept. 11 will add household confidence and inflation expectations. Consumer sentiment is expected near 51 after 51.7. One-year inflation expectations previously stood at 4%, and the 5-year measure at 3.3%. Continued elevation would matter more if higher pump prices begin to alter longer-term expectations rather than merely depress purchasing power.

SoftBank’s scheduled Sept. 15 repayment will test whether the bridge refinancing proceeds as announced. Paying the $25.9 billion balance removes a near-term maturity, but investors will still need the terms of any $10 billion to $20 billion bond sale and other permanent financing to assess the resulting leverage, collateral and maturity profile.

The Sept. 16 Fed decision remains the central U.S. policy event. Oil, PPI and CPI will determine whether stronger employment is accompanied by enough inflation pressure to produce the first increase in three years. The economic projections will show whether officials view a move as a discrete response or the start of additional tightening; markets already price at least two increases by the middle of 2027.

The BOJ follows on Sept. 18 with a quarter-point increase largely reflected in prices. The more consequential issue is whether Ueda validates expectations for faster subsequent action after Bessent’s campaign strengthened the yen. Guidance that preserves a roughly quarterly path would support the currency and increase the risk of further carry unwinds. A routine increase paired with caution could expose how much of the rally depended on expectations that policy would move faster than the BOJ itself intends.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as an energy shock and smaller-than-expected buyback lift long yields to multiyear highs
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries ended broadly 3 to 5 basis points cheaper after escalating U.S.-Iran hostilities lifted energy prices and Treasury announced a smaller long-dated buyback than aggressive market expectations. The 10-year yield rose 5.2 basis points to 4.842%, its highest since 2023, while the 30-year reached 5.29%. The curve steepened modestly as longer maturities led the decline after the buyback announcement.

The $6 billion maximum for the Sept. 10 purchase of 10- to 20-year securities was three times the prior schedule but below speculation of $8 billion to $10 billion. A well-received $39 billion 10-year auction later cleared about 1.5 basis points through the pre-sale yield, showing that higher yields could restore demand without reversing the session’s repricing.

Brent and WTI rose more than 4%, while European diesel’s premium over Brent widened to about $75 a barrel as Middle Eastern and Russian disruptions removed an estimated 4 million barrels a day of refined-product exports. Real yields accounted for most of the 10-year move, but breakevens also rose. Heavy corporate issuance still cleared, investment-grade spreads tightened clearly, and the contained equity and volatility response indicated a demand-driven repricing of duration rather than a funding seizure.
